summary: ```markdown # CLO Skill Workshop - Custom OBJ Outline ## Building the Model In the CLO, use the template to build the model. Start with these three small cubes. Take them out as an OPT. Then, put this OPT into the name line to use. ## Exporting the Model Be careful before you export. Place the model correctly first; it should be positioned in the middle. Check the model in the 3D window to ensure it shows the floor grid. ### Finding the Axes Identify the X-axis according to the floor grid. The name line will repeat along the X-axis. Refer to the provided picture for the direction of the three axes in the 3D window. ## Switching Angles Go back to the software and press the shortcut **5** to switch to the 5-angle view. In this view, the X-axis is horizontal. The name line will follow the blue, red, and yellow axes. ## Exporting to OPT Press the shortcut **5** again to switch to the 5-angle. Then, export it to OPT through the menu bar: **File > Export > OPT**. Select an address and save it to the desktop first. Remember the name of the file. ### Export OPT Window This is the export OPT window. Let's take a look at the information here. You can watch a video about the settings for exporting OPT. I won't cover all the options; let's set it directly. ## Export Settings Set a single target, which should be the thick one. Click on the unified UV coordinates. As long as the slow shooting picture is OK, you do not need the 發現 picture. Then, proceed to the next step. ### Saving the File Save it as a compressed package by clicking **OK**. The compressed package after export will be on the desktop. Right-click to unzip it. After unzipping, open the file to see the corresponding OPT file. ## Importing the OPT File Go back to the software and open the file for this skirt. Next, complete the strap of this skirt. Switch to the thick texture surface. Turn off the display of the inner line and the basic line. Zoom in to see the model's shoulder. ### Adding a Name Line Create a new name line by clicking **Add**. The OPT name line window will appear, displaying a setting area on the left and a preview window on the right. At this point, the preview window is still empty; you need to add the OPT file first. ## Adding the OPT File Click the **Browse** button to open the OPT file you just exported. The displayed length and width will correspond to the size of the OPT file, appearing in the preview window. ### Adjusting the Scale At this time, the scale is set to 0. The scale refers to the distance between each OPT unit. When exporting before, three small objects were exported together as a single unit. After modifying the scale to 10mm, the distance between the three small objects and the next group of small objects will change to 10mm. ## Modifying the Settings The scale can be adjusted above. You can also rotate the OPT on the X, Y, and Z axes. You do not need to select these options again, as they were already set at the beginning. Now, just import it directly and modify the settings. ### Adding Lines The scale refers to the number of lines added. The distance between the inner line and the outer line of the board is set to 0. Use the free line tool to add the number of lines to the board. The added lines will appear gray because the corresponding UV image has not yet been added. ## Finalizing the Model Select the number of lines in the object window, then click the **Browse** button to add the UV image. Repeat this process for the other shoulder boards. Finally, hide the bottom sheet. Click the fabric used for the shoulder board and change its opacity to 0. ### Clean Surface The surface of the fabric is now clean. The surface of the board is also clean. ```
